full_page.content:
1956, October 6
The following is a faithful transcription of the typed original by the Servant of God, Father Solanus Casey, C. F.M. Cap.
ST. BONAVENTURE MONASTERY 1740 Mt. Elliott Avenue DETROIT 7, MICHIGAN
October 6th, 1956 (Re: ) Carson Stone
Blessed be God in all His designs.
God bless you Dear Brother Gabriel.
God bless you and yours these days.
The above name - Carson Stone - is the name we were trying to think of this p.m. coming home from the doctor's. It was he from whom I received the remarkable letter that I have been anxious a- bout, and that has been on my mind and on my conscience for quite a time.
Let me first till you something about him so that I have cause enough for anyone to be ashamed of himself, to say the very least. .... World War II was fiercely on and the crazy nazies seem to have suc- ceeded in landing quite some of their assiciates for employment in Detroit, especially in the PKard Factory. .... You probably remember better than I do something of the sensation throughout, when Carson Stone as Head Inspecter of Amunition Department for that company, condemned a whole train-load of amunition just-about to be started for over-seas. Following that and such interference on Stone's part, drew all-kind of threatening letters to him which he seemed to pay little attention to
(unfinished draft)
